correctness.rationale: Exact integral-kernel/eigensystem reconstruction gives eigenvalues 1, 1/2, 1/10. For every t>0, minimizing the powered kernel over u,v∈[-1,1] is exactly minimizing a convex quadratic in p=|uv|∈[0,1], with equality witnessed at u=1,v=-p. The vertex equals 5^{t-1}; a strictly concave function for t≤1 and a single-turn derivative for t≥1 establish exactly two connected order-positivity intervals. The corresponding negative-kernel witnesses and the n=1 comparison complete the global theorem. A replayed standalone exact-rational checker passed 31,260 assertions, with infinite quantifiers proved analytically.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An evaluation matrix of a powered continuum integral operator is not the functional-calculus power of the evaluation matrix of the original operator. Finite doubly-nonnegative matrix-power preservation therefore cannot imply positivity of the continuum powered kernel. Integer iterates, which are Markov, also cannot imply preservation at every noninteger exponent. value.rationale: The canonical degree-two averaging operator is the first nontrivial polynomial Markov kernel to show failure and recovery of order positivity along its natural spectral-power family. The complete exact two-interval classification and explicit counterexample inputs settle a motivated finite-dimensional kernel-embedding question; nonmonotonicity after integer t=1 is structural and informs attempts to interpolate discrete positive approximation operators by positive continuous time.
